extracted.intended_audience: WIPO data users; IP statisticians; patent/plant-variety office staff; policymakers and researchers using IP statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology, definitions and counting rules used in the WIPO World Intellectual Property Indicators for plant variety applications/titles and geographical indications (GIs), including data-collection caveats and equivalence/counting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTE definition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a measure reported in procedural tables; no further elaboration on calculation given in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on comparability across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effort has been made to compile procedural data based on common definitions and concepts but procedural differences make it extremely difficult to fully harmonize such data. Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should not assume perfect harmonization; differences in procedures, omitted elements, or reporting practices may make direct comparisons misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete totals due to omission by offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of applications processed for any given office may be incomplete due to the omission of one or several elements by the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting office totals, consider possible under-reporting; consult footnotes and office-level notes for missing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examinations data footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) data are for formalities examinations only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where footnoted, counts may exclude substantive examination outcomes and refer only to formalities checks; check whether data refer to formalities versus substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for unavailable data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and statistical cells marked with '..' should be treated as non-reporting or missing rather than zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures and tables are drawn from WIPO's database as of August 2024; users can reference this source for updates or raw data queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office data versus origin data distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data, whereas applications filed by applicants at a national or regional office (resident applications) or at a foreign office (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses must distinguish office-based counts (where the application was received) from origin-based counts (where the applicant is domiciled). These produce different insights (destination vs applicant origin).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPVO counting rule for resident vs regional filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants domiciled within EU member states, filing at the CPVO regional office is regarded as a resident filing, when discussing office data, and such filings are regarded as regional filings, when discussing origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aggregating or comparing resident/abroad shares, treat CPVO filings according to this dual convention to avoid misclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of Retained EU PVRs for comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure comparability between offices, the 21,805 Plant Variety Rights (PVR) transferred to the UK by the European Union (referred to as 'Retained EU PVRs') that had been granted by the end of the transition period (December 31, 2020) as part of the Withdrawal Agreement between the UK and the EU have been excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing titles issued across years or offices, account for such administrative transfers that are excluded from analysis to avoid artificial spikes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not compare applications and titles for the same year
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that the grant or registration process takes time, therefore fluctuations in the volume of plant variety titles granted may be a consequence of changes in processing capacity or procedural delay. For this reason, data on applications for any given year should not be compared with data on titles issued that same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should account for time lags between application filing and title/grant issuance; use multi-year cohorts or lagged comparisons instead of year‑to‑year direct comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent applications / equivalent count concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states. See glossary for the definition of equivalent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where regional filings exist (e.g., CPVO), WIPO provides both absolute and 'equivalent' counts to reflect the multiplicative effect of regional filings on member-state coverage; use equivalent counts when assessing overall coverage across member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI definition and main function
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication (GI) is a sign identifying a good as having originated from a specific geographical area and possessing a given quality, reputation or other characteristic essentially attributable to that geographical origin. Thus, the main function of a GI is to identify goods whose quality, reputation or other characteristics are connected to their territory of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definitional standard underpins which products/labels are counted as GIs in the statistics and explains the policy rationale for GI protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal means for protecting GIs (counting implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs can be protected through a variety of legal means (e.g., sui generis systems, trademark law, regional systems, international agreements, other national legal means, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because protection mechanisms vary, WIPO aggregates across legal forms but notes that some countries cannot identify GIs protected through trademark systems, affecting completeness of national counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules to minimize double counting for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize double counting, GIs in force through the European Union (EU) regional system and the Lisbon System are counted once only, rather than multiplied by the number of member states party to each system. That notwithstanding, the overall total of around 58,600 will inevitably include a degree of double counting, as GIs in force through bilateral, plurilateral or multilateral agreements could potentially be included multiple times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware that WIPO applies specific deduplication steps (EU and Lisbon counted once) but residual double counting may remain; WIPO also reports an alternative total excluding international agreements (~23,400) for sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and treatment of partial/non-responding offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Data received by WIPO from a total of 86 national and regional authorities show... Two offices provided partial data, which are not included in this report. Six economies did not respond to the survey, but are included here because they have GIs in force through the Lisbon System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using WIPO aggregates, consult the coverage notes: some offices' data are partial or inferred via international systems; this affects totals and regional breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for 'n.a.' and other footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: n.a. indicates not applicable. .. indicates not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect these table conventions when parsing or interpreting the statistical tables; check footnotes (a),(b),(c),(d) for office-specific caveats (e.g., not UPOV membership, PVPA reporting, transfers).
